docs.title: 🧬 TrajGRN-Bench
docs.text:
Trajectory and Gene Regulatory Network Inference Benchmark

TrajGRN-Bench is a comprehensive benchmark of mechanistic models for joint gene regulatory network (GRN) and single-cell RNA-seq trajectory inference. We evaluate and compare multiple joint-inference approaches alongside complementary GRN and trajectory methods on simulated datasets.

docs.title: What We Provide
docs.text:
• Standardized Metrics

    Unified metrics for GRN inference (AUROC, AUPRC, etc.) and trajectory reconstruction (Wasserstein distance, EMD, etc.) — making fair comparisons across methods.

  • Flexible Configuration

    A single YAML config drives everything: which methods run, which datasets are used, what metrics to compute, and how results are stored.

  • Docker-Based Execution

    Each method runs in its own container. No dependency conflicts. Reproducible across any machine with Docker installed.

  • Interactive Rankings

    Auto-generated ranking tables and interactive visualizations let you explore method performance across all metrics at a glance.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# 1. Install the runner environment
conda env create -f environments/benchmark_runner.yml

# 2. Build method containers
make -f containers/Makefile -j4 all

# 3. Run the benchmark
bash benchmark_run.sh --config configs/benchmark.example.yaml

docs.title: Contributing to TrajGRN-Bench
docs.text: We welcome contributions! This guide covers how to contribute new methods, datasets, metrics, and improvements.

docs.title: Code of Conduct
docs.text: Please be respectful and constructive. We follow the Contributor Covenant.

docs.title: Ways to Contribute
docs.text:
• Add a Method

    Integrate a new GRN/trajectory inference method. See Adding a Method.

  • Add a Dataset

    Contribute a new benchmarking dataset. See Adding a Dataset.

  • :material-chart-box-plus:{ .lg .middle } Add a Metric

    Propose a new evaluation metric for GRN or trajectory quality.

  • Report a Bug

    Open an issue with detailed reproduction steps.

  • Improve Docs

    Fix typos, add examples, or clarify explanations.

docs.title: 1. Fork and Clone
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/TrajGRN-Bench.git
cd TrajGRN-Bench
git remote add upstream https://github.com/YOUR_ORG/TrajGRN-Bench.git

docs.title: 2. Create a Branch
docs.text: git checkout -b feature/my-new-method

docs.title: 3. Make Your Changes
docs.text:
Follow the relevant guide:

  • Adding a Method
  • Adding a Dataset
  • Methods Registry

docs.title: 4. Test
docs.text:
# Run the full benchmark with your changes
bash benchmark_run.sh --config configs/benchmark.example.yaml

# Build and serve documentation locally
pip install mkdocs-material mkdocstrings
mkdocs serve

docs.title: 5. Submit a Pull Request
docs.text:
1. Push your branch
  2. Open a PR against main
  3. Describe your changes and why they're needed
  4. Link any related issues

docs.title: Pull Request Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Method/dataset follows I/O specification
  • [ ] Entry added to methods_registry.yaml (if applicable)
  • [ ] Conda environment file provided (if new method)
  • [ ] Docker image builds successfully
  • [ ] Benchmark runs complete without errors
  • [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
  • [ ] Tests pass (if applicable)

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
• Follow PEP 8
  • Use type hints where practical
  • Document functions with Google-style docstrings
  • Use pathlib.Path for file paths

docs.title: Shell Scripts
docs.text:
• Use #!/bin/bash shebang
  • Quote all variable expansions: "$var"
  • Use [[ ]] for conditionals
  • Run through shellcheck

docs.title: YAML
docs.text:
• Use 2-space indentation
  • Quote strings that contain special characters
  • Include comments for non-obvious settings

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
We use MkDocs Material. To contribute to docs:

pip install mkdocs-material "mkdocstrings[python]"
cd TrajGRN-Bench
mkdocs serve

Visit http://localhost:8000 to preview.

docs.title: Adding a Metric
docs.text:
To add a new evaluation metric:

  1. Implement the metric function in post_analysis/metrics_grn.py or post_analysis/metrics_cells.py
  2. Register it in post_analysis/compute_metrics.py
  3. Update ranking_table.py to display the new metric
  4. Add documentation in this guide

docs.title: Development Overview
docs.text: This section covers how to extend TrajGRN-Bench with new methods, datasets, metrics, and simulators.

docs.title: Methods Registry
docs.text:
The single source of truth for all method metadata is methods_registry.yaml (in the repo root). Every downstream tool derives its configuration from this file:

  • benchmark_run.sh — default enabled methods list
  • single_run.sh — per-method execution parameters
  • ranking_table.py — capabilities table
  • containers/Makefile — Docker image build targets
  • configs/benchmark.schema.json — config validation

Registry API Reference →

docs.title: Method Entrypoints
docs.text:
Each method has a standardized entrypoint script that receives:

  1. Input AnnData file path
  2. Output directory path
  3. Training timepoints
  4. Output mode specification
  5. Optional parameters (KO genes, etc.)

All methods follow the I/O specification for consistency.

docs.title: Simulators
docs.text:
Simulators generate synthetic scRNA-seq data for benchmarking. Located in simulator/, they support:

  • Harissa — default mechanistic simulator
  • BoolODE — Boolean network-based simulator
  • SERGIO — (in progress) gene regulation simulator

docs.title: Adding a New Dataset
docs.text: This guide explains how to prepare and integrate a new benchmarking dataset.

docs.title: Dataset Format
docs.text: Datasets must be in AnnData (HDF5) format (.h5ad). See the full I/O specification for the complete schema.

docs.title: Minimal Requirements
docs.text:
adata
├── .X          # Gene expression matrix [n_cells × n_genes] (dense or sparse)
├── .obs        # Cell metadata (must contain 'timepoint' or 'time' column)
├── .var        # Gene metadata (index = gene names)
└── .uns        # Optional: 'simulation' flag, ground-truth network, etc.

docs.title: From a CSV / TSV
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
import scanpy as sc
import anndata

# Load expression matrix
expr = pd.read_csv("expression.csv", index_col=0)  # genes × cells

# Load cell metadata
meta = pd.read_csv("metadata.csv", index_col=0)     # cells × attributes

# Create AnnData
adata = anndata.AnnData(X=expr.T.values, obs=meta, var=pd.DataFrame(index=expr.index))

# Ensure timepoint column exists
assert "timepoint" in adata.obs.columns, "Metadata must have 'timepoint' column"

# Save
adata.write_h5ad("benchmark/data/my_dataset.h5ad")

docs.title: From a Seurat Object (R)
docs.text:
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratDisk)

# Load Seurat object
obj <- readRDS("my_data.rds")

# Convert and save
SaveH5Seurat(obj, filename = "my_data.h5seurat")
Convert("my_data.h5seurat", dest = "h5ad")

docs.title: Timepoint Files
docs.text:
Create NumPy arrays for train/test timepoint splits:

import numpy as np

# Define which timepoints are training vs test
# Format: [[timepoint_id, timepoint_value], ...]
train_tps = np.array([[0, 0.0], [1, 1.0], [2, 2.0]])
test_tps = np.array([[3, 3.0], [4, 4.0]])

np.save("benchmark/data/my_train_tps.npy", train_tps)
np.save("benchmark/data/my_test_tps.npy", test_tps)

docs.title: Ground Truth (Optional)
docs.text:
If you have a ground-truth GRN:

# N×N adjacency matrix with gene names as index/columns
grn = pd.read_csv("ground_truth_grn.csv", index_col=0)
# Place in benchmark/data/True/ or alongside your dataset

docs.title: Dataset Placement
docs.text:
Place your files in the standard locations:

benchmark/data/
├── my_dataset.h5ad          # Your AnnData file
├── my_train_tps.npy         # Training timepoints
├── my_test_tps.npy          # Test timepoints
└── True/                    # Ground truth (optional)
    └── my_dataset_grn.csv   # Ground-truth GRN

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Add your dataset to the benchmark config:

data:
  adata_files:
    - benchmark/data/my_dataset.h5ad
  train_tps: benchmark/data/my_train_tps.npy
  test_tps: benchmark/data/my_test_tps.npy

For multiple datasets:

data:
  adata_files:
    - benchmark/data/data_1.h5ad
    - benchmark/data/my_dataset.h5ad

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Verify your dataset loads correctly:

import scanpy as sc
import numpy as np

adata = sc.read_h5ad("benchmark/data/my_dataset.h5ad")
print(f"Shape: {adata.shape}")
print(f"Timepoints: {adata.obs['timepoint'].unique()}")
print(f"Genes: {adata.var_names[:5].tolist()}")
assert "timepoint" in adata.obs.columns or "time" in adata.obs.columns

docs.title: Adding a New Method
docs.text: This guide walks you through integrating a new inference method into TrajGRN-Bench. In most cases, you only need to touch two files: the method entrypoint script and methods_registry.yaml.

docs.title: 1. Write the Method Entrypoint Script
docs.text:
Create a Python (or bash) script in methods/<your_method>/ that follows the standard CLI convention:

python methods/<your_method>/infer.py \
    --adata <input.h5ad> \
    --output_dir <output_dir> \
    --train_tps <train_tps.npy> \
    --test_tps <test_tps.npy> \
    --output_mode full_test \
    [--ko_genes GENE1,GENE2]

Your script must produce:

File Required Description predicted_grn.csv If GRN-capable \(N \times N\) adjacency matrix, CSV, genes as row/col names simulated_adata.h5ad If trajectory-capable AnnData with .X containing simulated expression .done Always Empty marker file indicating successful completion

See the full Method I/O Specification for details.

Minimal Python entrypoint template 
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal method entrypoint for TrajGRN-Bench."""
import argparse, os, numpy as np, pandas as pd, scanpy as sc

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--adata", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output_dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--train_tps", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--test_tps", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output_mode", default="full_test")
    parser.add_argument("--ko_genes", default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(args.output_dir, exist_ok=True)

    # Load data
    adata = sc.read_h5ad(args.adata)
    train_tps = np.load(args.train_tps)

    # --- Your method logic here ---
    grn_matrix = np.random.randn(adata.n_vars, adata.n_vars)

    # Save GRN
    pd.DataFrame(grn_matrix, index=adata.var_names,
                 columns=adata.var_names).to_csv(
                 os.path.join(args.output_dir, "predicted_grn.csv"))

    # Mark completion
    open(os.path.join(args.output_dir, ".done"), "w").close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: 2. Create a Conda Environment File
docs.text:
Create environments/<your_method>.yml with all dependencies:

name: your_method
channels:
  - conda-forge
  - defaults
dependencies:
  - python=3.10
  - numpy
  - pandas
  - scanpy
  - pip
  - pip:
      - your-method-package

docs.title: 3. Register in methods_registry.yaml
docs.text:
Add your method under the methods: key:

methods:
  # ... existing methods ...

  YourMethod:
    display_name: Your Method
    description: >
      Short description of your method and what it does.
    github: https://github.com/yourorg/your-method
    publication: "Your Paper (Year) DOI:..."
    entrypoint:
      type: python
      script: methods/your_method/infer.py
      pass_output_mode: true
      pass_ko_genes: false
      supports_perturbation_training: false
    execution:
      default_runner: docker
      conda_env: your_method
      container:
        image: benchmark/yourmethod:latest
        env_file: environments/your_method.yml
        env_name: your_method
    capabilities:
      grn_inference: true
      trajectory_reconstruction: true
      perturbation_training: false

Then add YourMethod to the iteration_order list at the bottom of the file.

docs.title: 4. Build the Docker Image
docs.text:
docker build -f containers/docker/Dockerfile \
  --build-arg ENV_FILE=environments/your_method.yml \
  --build-arg ENV_NAME=your_method \
  -t benchmark/yourmethod:latest .

docs.title: 5. Test Locally
docs.text:
# Test your entrypoint directly
python methods/your_method/infer.py \
  --adata benchmark/data/data_1.h5ad \
  --output_dir /tmp/test_output \
  --train_tps benchmark/data/train_tps.npy \
  --test_tps benchmark/data/test_tps.npy \
  --output_mode full_test

# Test via the benchmark runner (single method)
python benchmark_run_config.py --config configs/benchmark.example.yaml

docs.title: 6. Verify Metrics
docs.text:
python post_analysis/compute_metrics.py \
  --methods-dir benchmark/outputs_methods/<run_name>/YourMethod \
  --output-dir /tmp/test_metrics

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Entrypoint script follows CLI convention
  • [ ] Produces predicted_grn.csv (if GRN-capable)
  • [ ] Produces simulated_adata.h5ad (if trajectory-capable)
  • [ ] Creates .done marker on completion
  • [ ] Conda environment file in environments/
  • [ ] Entry added to methods_registry.yaml
  • [ ] Entry added to iteration_order in registry
  • [ ] Docker image builds successfully
  • [ ] Metrics compute correctly

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text:
• Check the Method I/O Specification
  • See examples in methods/CardamomOT/, methods/flecs/, etc.
  • Open an issue on GitHub

docs.title: Methods Registry
docs.text: The methods_registry.yaml file is the single source of truth for all method metadata in TrajGRN-Bench. Every downstream consumer derives its configuration from this file.

docs.title: Why a Registry?
docs.text:
Before the registry, adding a new method required touching 6+ files:

  • benchmark_run.sh — default method list
  • single_run.sh — entrypoint parameters
  • ranking_table.py — capabilities
  • containers/Makefile — build targets
  • containers/build_all.sh — build targets
  • configs/benchmark.schema.json — validation

Now, you only need to edit one file: methods_registry.yaml.

docs.title: Registry Structure
docs.text:
schema_version: 1

methods:
  MethodName:
    display_name: Human-Readable Name
    description: >
      Multi-line description of the method.
    github: https://github.com/org/repo
    publication: "Citation string"

    entrypoint:
      type: python               # python | bash
      script: methods/foo/run.py
      pass_output_mode: true     # Pass --output_mode flag
      pass_ko_genes: false       # Pass --ko_genes flag
      supports_perturbation_training: false
      extra_args:                # Always-passed CLI args
        - "--flag"
        - "value"

    execution:
      default_runner: docker     # docker | conda | apptainer
      conda_env: env_name
      container:
        image: benchmark/method:latest
        env_file: environments/method.yml
        env_name: env_name

    capabilities:
      grn_inference: true
      trajectory_reconstruction: true
      perturbation_training: false

iteration_order:
  - MethodOne
  - MethodTwo
  # ... controls display order in tables

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
The utils/methods_registry.py module provides programmatic access:

from utils.methods_registry import (
    get_registry,
    get_method,
    get_method_keys,
    get_capabilities_table,
    get_execution_config,
)

# Get all registered methods
registry = get_registry()
print(registry["methods"].keys())

# Get a specific method
method = get_method("FLeCS")
print(method["capabilities"])

# Get capabilities as a DataFrame
caps = get_capabilities_table()
print(caps)

# Get execution config (merges registry + user overrides)
exec_cfg = get_execution_config(user_overrides={...})

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
For shell scripts (used by single_run.sh, build_all.sh, etc.):

# List all method keys
python utils/methods_registry.py keys

# Get entrypoint info for a method
python utils/methods_registry.py entrypoint FLeCS

# Get full execution config as JSON
python utils/methods_registry.py execution-json

# Get capabilities as JSON
python utils/methods_registry.py capabilities-json

# Get default enabled methods JSON
python utils/methods_registry.py default-methods-json

# List container image build specs
python utils/methods_registry.py container-images

# Check if a method supports perturbation training
python utils/methods_registry.py supports-perturbation FLeCS

# Get the conda environment name for a method
python utils/methods_registry.py conda-env FLeCS

# Get the runner mode (docker/conda/apptainer)
python utils/methods_registry.py runner-mode FLeCS

# Get the container image name
python utils/methods_registry.py container-image FLeCS

docs.title: Auto-Generated Artifacts
docs.text:
When you run python utils/methods_registry.py with certain flags, it generates:

Consumer How it uses the registry single_run.sh Calls _registry_query which invokes registry CLI benchmark_run.sh python utils/methods_registry.py default-methods-json ranking_table.py from utils.methods_registry import get_capabilities_table benchmark_run_config.py build_execution_json() merges registry + overrides configs/benchmark.schema.json run_methods propertyNames enum containers/Makefile Targets auto-generated from registry containers/build_all.sh ALL_IMAGES auto-generated docs/_scripts/generate_methods.py Auto-generates method pages

docs.title: "conda: command not found"
docs.text:
Install Miniconda:

wget https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh
bash Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh

docs.title: "Docker daemon not running"
docs.text:
Start Docker:

sudo systemctl start docker        # Linux
# Or use Docker Desktop on macOS/Windows

Verify:

docker run hello-world

docs.title: "permission denied" when running Docker
docs.text:
Add yourself to the docker group:

sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
newgrp docker

docs.title: Conda environment creation fails
docs.text:
Try using Mamba (faster solver):

conda install -c conda-forge mamba
mamba env create -f environments/benchmark_runner.yml

docs.title: Container build fails with "no space left on device"
docs.text:
Docker images can be large. Clean up:

docker system prune -a

docs.title: Method fails with "Killed" or OOM
docs.text:
The method ran out of memory. Options:

  1. Reduce the dataset size
  2. Subsample cells (use train_data: subsample_full)
  3. Increase Docker memory limit in Docker Desktop settings

docs.title: ".done file not found" error
docs.text: This means the method crashed or was interrupted. Check the method's log output in the terminal. Re-run with restart_mode: rerun to force re-execution.

docs.title: Container can't access GPU
docs.text:
Ensure NVIDIA Container Toolkit is installed:

nvidia-container-cli info

If not installed:

# Ubuntu/Debian
distribution=$(. /etc/os-release;echo $ID$VERSION_ID)
curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/gpgkey | sudo apt-key add -
curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/$distribution/nvidia-docker.list | \
  sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nvidia-docker.list
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-container-toolkit
sudo systemctl restart docker

docs.title: "AnnData file not found" or "KeyError: timepoint"
docs.text:
Your dataset is missing the required structure. Verify:

import scanpy as sc
adata = sc.read_h5ad("benchmark/data/data_1.h5ad")
print(adata.obs.columns)  # Should include 'timepoint' or 'time'
print(adata.shape)

docs.title: Why are some metrics NaN?
docs.text: A method may not support certain output types. For example, GENIE3 doesn't produce trajectory outputs, so cell-level metrics will be NaN.

docs.title: How do I compare results across runs?
docs.text:
Use post_analysis/compute_metrics.py with multiple run directories:

python post_analysis/compute_metrics.py \
  --runs run_1 run_2 run_3 \
  --output comparison.csv

docs.title: Ranking table is empty
docs.text: Ensure both grn_metrics.csv and cell_metrics.csv exist in the metrics output directory. Run compute_metrics.py first if needed.

docs.title: How do I add a new method?
docs.text: See Adding a Method. The short version: add an entry to methods_registry.yaml and write an entrypoint script.

docs.title: Can I use a language other than Python?
docs.text: Yes. Set entrypoint.type: bash in the registry and write a bash script that wraps your method. The script must accept the same CLI arguments.

docs.title: How do I test my method without Docker?
docs.text: Set execution.default_runner: conda in your config and create the conda environment. Run the entrypoint script directly for debugging.

docs.title: Still Stuck?
docs.text:
• Check existing GitHub Issues
  • Open a new issue with:
    • Full error message
    • Your config file (sanitized)
    • OS and Docker version
    • Steps to reproduce

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This guide walks you through setting up TrajGRN-Bench on your machine.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Linux or macOS (Windows via WSL2)
  • Docker (for containerized method execution)
  • Conda (Miniconda or Anaconda, for the runner environment)

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_ORG/TrajGRN-Bench.git
cd TrajGRN-Bench

docs.title: Step 2: Create the Runner Environment
docs.text:
The runner environment manages simulations, orchestrates method calls, and computes metrics. It does not need method-specific dependencies — those live inside Docker containers.

conda env create -f environments/benchmark_runner.yml
conda activate benchmark_runner
Verify the installation 
python -c "import anndata, scanpy, pandas; print('Runner env OK')"

docs.title: Step 3: Build Method Containers
docs.text:
Each method runs in its own Docker container. Build all images at once:

Using Make (recommended)Using the shell scriptManual (one at a time) 
# Build all images (4 parallel builds)
make -f containers/Makefile -j4 all

# Or build a single method
make -f containers/Makefile flecs

bash containers/build_all.sh -j 4

docker build -f containers/docker/Dockerfile \
  --build-arg ENV_FILE=environments/flecs_cpu.yml \
  --build-arg ENV_NAME=flecs \
  -t benchmark/flecs:latest .
List available images 
python utils/methods_registry.py container-images

docs.title: Step 4: Verify the Setup
docs.text:
Run a minimal test to verify everything works:

bash benchmark_run.sh --config configs/benchmark.example.yaml

The first run will download datasets and may take a while. Check benchmark/outputs_metrics/ for result files.

docs.title: Optional: Conda-Only Execution (Legacy)
docs.text:
If you don't want to use Docker, you can create method-specific conda environments directly:

# Create method environments (without Docker)
conda env create -f environments/flecs_cpu.yml
conda env create -f environments/sc_dynamic.yml
conda env create -f environments/reference_fitting.yml
conda env create -f environments/cardamom_ot.yml

# Run with conda runner
python benchmark_run_config.py --config configs/benchmark.example.yaml

Then set execution.default_runner: conda in your config file.

Warning

Conda environments may conflict with each other. Docker is the recommended approach for reproducible runs.

docs.title: GPU Support
docs.text:
For GPU-accelerated methods, use the GPU environment files:

docker build -f containers/docker/Dockerfile \
  --build-arg ENV_FILE=environments/flecs_gpu.yml \
  --build-arg ENV_NAME=flecs \
  -t benchmark/flecs:latest .

Ensure you have the NVIDIA Container Toolkit installed.

docs.title: Methods Overview
docs.text: TrajGRN-Bench includes a diverse set of methods spanning mechanistic models, deep learning, optimal transport, and classical baselines.

docs.title: Joint GRN + Trajectory Methods
docs.text: These methods jointly infer both the gene regulatory network and cellular trajectories from time-course scRNA-seq data.

docs.title: FLeCS
docs.text:
Repository

Functional and Learnable Cell dynamicS — a scalable gene-network-based differential-equation model that incorporates network structure to infer regulatory dynamics and simulate single-cell trajectories.

  • Publication: arXiv:2503.20027 (2025)
  • GRN: Trajectory: Perturbation:
  • Variant: FLeCS-TPs

docs.title: FLeCS-TPs
docs.text:
Repository

FLeCS variant that forces timepoint alignment during training.

  • Publication: arXiv:2503.20027 (2025)
  • GRN: Trajectory: Perturbation:

docs.title: Reference Fitting
docs.text:
Repository

Joint trajectory and network inference via reference fitting; leverages dynamical and perturbational single-cell data to jointly infer trajectories and directed/signed networks using min-entropy estimation.

  • Publication: arXiv:2409.06879 (2024)
  • GRN: Trajectory: Perturbation:

docs.title: CardamomOT
docs.text:
Repository

Mechanistic GRN inference that fits stochastic models to time-course scRNA-seq and then simulates the calibrated model. Designed to produce interpretable kinetic parameters and synthetic trajectories for benchmarking.

  • Publication: bioRxiv (2026) DOI:10.64898/2026.03.31.715390
  • GRN: Trajectory: Perturbation:

docs.title: RENGE
docs.text:
Repository

REgulatory Network inference using GEne perturbation data; infers GRNs from time-series single-cell data using a kinetic model with hyperparameter optimization. Optionally leverages CRISPR perturbation (KO) data when available.

  • Publication: Communications Biology (2023) DOI:10.1038/s42003-023-05594-4
  • GRN: Trajectory: Perturbation:

docs.title: GENIE3
docs.text:
Repository

Tree-ensemble regression approach (Random Forests) for gene regulatory network inference from expression data; widely used baseline for GRN reconstruction.

  • Publication: PLoS ONE (2010) DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0012776
  • GRN: Trajectory: Perturbation:

docs.title: Pearson (coexpression)
docs.text:
Local script: methods/pearson/inference_pearson.py

Computes pairwise Pearson correlation between genes as a naive GRN scoring baseline.

  • Publication: —
  • GRN: Trajectory: Perturbation:

docs.title: scNODE
docs.text:
Repository

A VAE + Neural ODE generative model that learns continuous-time dynamics on a latent manifold to predict and simulate single-cell transcriptomic trajectories.

  • Publication: bioRxiv 2023 DOI:10.1101/2023.11.22.568346
  • GRN: Trajectory: Perturbation:

docs.title: TrajectoryNet
docs.text:
Repository

Continuous normalizing-flow / optimal-transport-based model that learns continuous paths between distributions for modeling cellular dynamics and sampling predictions at arbitrary timepoints.

  • Publication: ICML 2020, arXiv:2002.04461
  • GRN: Trajectory: Perturbation:

docs.title: Waddington-OT
docs.text:
Repository

Optimal-transport-based approach (Waddington-OT) that computes transport maps between timepoints and interpolates gene-expression clouds to reconstruct trajectories.

  • Publication: Cell (2019) DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2019.01.006
  • GRN: Trajectory: Perturbation:

docs.title: Method Input/Output Specification
docs.text: This page documents the standardized input/output formats for all methods in TrajGRN-Bench. Every method must follow these conventions.

docs.title: CLI Convention
docs.text:
All method entrypoints must accept these arguments:

python <script> \
    --adata <path>          # Input AnnData (.h5ad)
    --output_dir <path>      # Where to write results
    --train_tps <path>       # Training timepoints (.npy)
    --test_tps <path>        # Test timepoints (.npy)
    --output_mode <mode>     # full_full | full_train | full_test | no_traj
    [--ko_genes <genes>]     # Optional: comma-separated KO target genes

docs.title: Input: AnnData
docs.text:
adata
├── .X          # Gene expression [n_cells × n_genes] — dense or sparse
├── .obs        # Cell metadata — must have 'timepoint' or 'time'
├── .var        # Gene metadata — index = gene names
└── .uns        # Optional unstructured metadata

docs.title: Input: Timepoints
docs.text:
NumPy array, shape (n_timepoints, 2):

# [[timepoint_id, timepoint_value], ...]
[[0, 0.0], [1, 1.0], [2, 2.0]]

Filter training data: adata[adata.obs['timepoint'].isin(train_tps[:, 1])]

docs.title: predicted_grn.csv (if GRN-capable)
docs.text:
\(N \times N\) adjacency matrix with gene names as both row and column labels:

, GeneA, GeneB, GeneC
GeneA, 0.0, 0.8, -0.3
GeneB, 0.1, 0.0, 0.5
GeneC, 0.0, 0.2, 0.0
  • Values represent edge weights (positive = activation, negative = inhibition)
  • Must be symmetric? No — directed networks are allowed

docs.title: simulated_adata.h5ad (if trajectory-capable)
docs.text:
AnnData object with simulated expression in .X:

import scanpy as sc
adata_sim = sc.read_h5ad("simulated_adata.h5ad")
# adata_sim.X shape: [n_simulated_cells × n_genes]
# adata_sim.obs should contain 'timepoint'

docs.title: .done marker (always required)
docs.text:
An empty file signaling successful completion:

touch <output_dir>/.done

docs.title: Optional Outputs
docs.text: File Description latent_representation/ Method-specific latent embeddings kinetic_parameters.csv Inferred kinetic rates per gene *.png Diagnostic plots

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
See working implementations in:

  • methods/CardamomOT/infer_test.py — Python entrypoint
  • methods/flecs/flecs_train.py — Python entrypoint with extra args
  • methods/scnode/scnode.py — Python entrypoint
  • methods/pearson/inference_pearson.py — Simple baseline example

docs.title: Results & Rankings Gallery
docs.text: This page displays benchmark results and rankings. Results are auto-generated from data files placed in docs/results_data/.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Run a benchmark: bash benchmark_run.sh --config configs/benchmark.example.yaml
  2. Export results to the docs data directory: 
    python docs/_scripts/export_results.py \
  --metrics-dir benchmark/outputs_metrics/<your_run> \
  --output-dir docs/results_data/<your_run>
  3. Rebuild the docs: mkdocs build

Results appear below automatically.

No results data yet. Run a benchmark and export results to populate this page.

docs.title: Step 1: Run a Benchmark
docs.text: bash benchmark_run.sh --config configs/benchmark.example.yaml

docs.title: Step 2: Export Results
docs.text:
python docs/_scripts/export_results.py \
  --metrics-dir benchmark/outputs_metrics/my_run_future_full_test \
  --output-dir docs/results_data/my_run \
  --label "My First Run" \
  --description "Full benchmark with all methods on dataset 1"

docs.title: Step 3: Rebuild Docs
docs.text: mkdocs build  # or mkdocs serve for preview

docs.title: Result Metadata Format
docs.text:
Each result directory contains:

docs/results_data/my_run/
├── metadata.yaml        # Run description, date, config summary
├── grn_metrics.csv      # GRN metric scores
├── cell_metrics.csv     # Cell/trajectory metric scores
├── gene_metrics.csv     # Gene-level metric scores (optional)
├── ranking_table.png    # Visual ranking (optional)
└── notes.md             # Free-form notes (optional)

metadata.yaml example:

label: "Full Benchmark v1.0"
description: "All methods, dataset 1, future prediction mode"
date: "2026-07-03"
config:
  train_data: future
  output_mode: full_test
  simulator: harissa
methods:
  - FLeCS
  - scNODE
  - CardamomOT
  - reference_fitting
  - GENIE3
  - PEARSON

docs.title: Interactive Ranking
docs.text: Results are rendered as interactive Plotly charts — hover for details, click legend items to toggle methods, and use the toolbar to zoom/pan/export.

docs.title: Running Benchmarks
docs.text: This guide covers how to run benchmarks, interpret the configuration, and understand the output.

docs.title: Quick Run
docs.text:
The simplest way to run a benchmark is through the shell script:

bash benchmark_run.sh --config configs/benchmark.example.yaml

This single command will:

  1. Load the specified dataset(s)
  2. Run each enabled method on the training data
  3. Compute GRN and trajectory metrics
  4. Generate ranking tables and visualizations

docs.title: Run Modes
docs.text: TrajGRN-Bench supports several training/evaluation modes, controlled by train_data and output_mode:

docs.title: Training Modes (train_data)
docs.text: Mode Description full Train on all available timepoints future Train on only the first \(N\) timepoints, predict the rest leave-one-out Leave one intermediate timepoint out; run all combinations subsample_full All timepoints but only 66% of cells at each

docs.title: Output Modes (output_mode)
docs.text: Mode Description full_full Simulate all timepoints from \(t_0\) full_train Simulate only training timepoints from \(t_0\) full_test Simulate test timepoints from last training timepoint no_traj Skip trajectory simulation (GRN-only evaluation)

docs.title: Simulation Modes
docs.text: Mode Description simul_replicates Generate replicate simulations simul_ko Simulate gene knockouts false Use existing data (no simulation)

docs.title: Selecting Methods
docs.text:
Methods are selected via the run_methods section in your config:

run_methods:
  FLeCS: "1"
  scNODE: "1"
  CardamomOT: "1"
  GENIE3: "1"
  PEARSON: "1"

Set a method to "0" to disable it, or omit it entirely.

To see all available methods:

python utils/methods_registry.py keys

docs.title: Output Structure
docs.text:
After a successful run, you'll find:

benchmark/
├── outputs_methods/
│   └── <run_name>_<mode>/
│       ├── <method>/
│       │   ├── predicted_grn.csv       # Inferred GRN adjacency matrix
│       │   ├── simulated_adata.h5ad    # Simulated trajectory (AnnData)
│       │   ├── latent_representation/  # Method-specific latent outputs
│       │   └── .done                    # Completion marker
│       └── ...
├── outputs_metrics/
│   └── <run_name>_<mode>/
│       ├── grn_metrics.csv             # GRN inference scores
│       ├── cell_metrics.csv            # Trajectory reconstruction scores
│       ├── ranking_table.png           # Visual ranking chart
│       └── method_capabilities.csv     # Method feature matrix

docs.title: Running with Python Directly
docs.text:
If you prefer Python over the shell wrapper:

conda run -n benchmark_runner python benchmark_run_config.py --config configs/benchmark.example.yaml

docs.title: Restart / Resume
docs.text:
By default, the benchmark skips methods that have a .done marker:

execution:
  restart_mode: save    # Skip completed methods
  # restart_mode: rerun  # Re-run everything from scratch

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:

  • Interpret your results
  • Add a new method

docs.title: Configuration Guide
docs.text: TrajGRN-Bench uses a single YAML configuration file to control every aspect of a benchmark run. This page documents all available options.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: The configuration is validated against a JSON schema at configs/benchmark.schema.json. Use an editor with YAML schema support (VS Code, PyCharm) for auto-completion and validation.

docs.title: run_name
docs.text:
A human-readable name for this benchmark run. Used in output directory names.

run_name: my_experiment

docs.title: train_data and output_mode
docs.text:
Control which data is used for training and what the methods should output:

train_data: future          # full | future | leave-one-out | subsample_full
output_mode: full_test      # full_full | full_train | full_test | no_traj

docs.title: simulation
docs.text:
Controls data generation:

simulation:
  mode: simul_replicates    # simul_replicates | simul_ko | false
  simulator_backend: harissa # harissa | boolode | sergio
  replicates_number: 3
  ko_output_genes: none     # none | all | "GENE1,GENE2"

docs.title: data
docs.text:
Input data configuration:

data:
  adata_files:              # Paths to input AnnData files
    - benchmark/data/data_1.h5ad
  train_tps: benchmark/data/train_tps.npy
  test_tps: benchmark/data/test_tps.npy
  degradation_rates: null   # Optional path to degradation rates file

docs.title: run_methods
docs.text:
Which methods to run ("1" = enabled, "0" = disabled):

run_methods:
  FLeCS: "1"
  FLeCS-TPs: "0"
  scNODE: "1"
  CardamomOT: "1"
  reference_fitting: "1"
  GENIE3: "1"
  PEARSON: "1"
  WOT: "0"
  TrajectoryNet: "0"
  RENGE: "0"

Discover available methods

python utils/methods_registry.py keys

docs.title: execution
docs.text:
Controls how methods are executed:

execution:
  default_runner: docker              # docker | conda | apptainer
  restart_mode: save                  # save (skip completed) | rerun
  conda_envs: {}                      # Only for conda runner
  container_images: {}                # Only for docker/apptainer runner

docs.title: metrics
docs.text:
Which metrics to compute:

metrics:
  grn: true           # Compute GRN metrics
  cell: true           # Compute cell-level trajectory metrics
  gene: true           # Compute gene-level metrics

docs.title: output
docs.text:
Output paths:

output:
  methods_dir: benchmark/outputs_methods
  metrics_dir: benchmark/outputs_metrics

docs.title: future
docs.text:
Settings for future-prediction mode:

future:
  start_tp: 2        # Timepoint index where test period begins

docs.title: perturbation
docs.text:
Perturbation training settings:

perturbation:
  training: false     # Enable perturbation-training variants

docs.title: Advanced: Method-Specific Overrides
docs.text:
You can override execution settings per method:

execution:
  default_runner: docker
  method_runners:
    GENIE3: conda          # Run GENIE3 in conda, everything else in Docker
  container_images:
    flecs: benchmark/flecs:latest
  conda_envs:
    GENIE3: genie3_env

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Validate your config against the schema:

python -c "
import yaml, jsonschema
with open('configs/benchmark.example.yaml') as f:
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)
with open('configs/benchmark.schema.json') as f:
    schema = json.load(f)
jsonschema.validate(cfg, schema)
print('Config is valid!')
"

docs.title: Understanding Results
docs.text: This page explains how to interpret the output of a benchmark run.

docs.title: Output Files
docs.text:
After running a benchmark, you'll find results in benchmark/outputs_metrics/<run_name>_<mode>/:

File Description grn_metrics.csv GRN inference performance per method cell_metrics.csv Trajectory reconstruction performance per method ranking_table.png Visual ranking of all methods method_capabilities.csv Method feature/capability matrix

docs.title: GRN Metrics
docs.text:
GRN (Gene Regulatory Network) metrics evaluate how well each method recovers the true regulatory network:

Metric Range Description AUROC [0, 1] Area Under the ROC Curve — overall edge detection AUPRC [0, 1] Area Under Precision-Recall Curve — better for imbalanced networks AUPRC Signed [0, 1] AUPRC considering edge sign (activation vs. inhibition) Precision@K [0, 1] Precision among top-K predicted edges

Higher is better for all GRN metrics.

docs.title: Cell / Trajectory Metrics
docs.text:
These metrics evaluate how well methods reconstruct cellular trajectories:

Metric Range Description Wasserstein Distance \([0, \infty)\) Earth Mover's Distance between predicted and true distributions MMD \([0, \infty)\) Maximum Mean Discrepancy — kernel-based distribution distance R² (per gene) \((-\infty, 1]\) Gene-wise correlation between predicted and true expression

Lower is better for distance-based metrics; higher is better for R².

docs.title: Gene-Level Metrics
docs.text:
Gene-specific metrics evaluate per-gene prediction quality:

Metric Range Description Gene-wise R² \((-\infty, 1]\) Per-gene prediction accuracy Gene-wise MSE \([0, \infty)\) Per-gene mean squared error

docs.title: Ranking Table
docs.text:
The ranking table (ranking_table.png) provides a visual summary:

  • Rows: Methods
  • Columns: Metric categories (GRN, Cell, Gene, Runtime)
  • Circles: Proportional to normalized scores — larger/darker = better
  • Number in circle: Rank position (only top-N shown)
  • Hollow grey circle: Method does not produce this output type

docs.title: Interactive Visualizations
docs.text:
If you ran with visualization enabled, you'll also find:

  • post_analysis/visualizations.py — Static and interactive plots
  • Per-method diagnostic plots in each method's output directory

docs.title: Exporting for the Docs
docs.text:
To include your results in the documentation (see Results Gallery):

# Export results to the docs data directory
python docs/_scripts/export_results.py \
  --metrics-dir benchmark/outputs_metrics/my_run_future_full_test \
  --output-dir docs/results_data/my_run

Then rebuild the docs. The results will appear automatically in the gallery.

docs.title: Comparing Runs
docs.text:
To compare multiple benchmark runs:

python post_analysis/compute_metrics.py \
  --runs run_1 run_2 run_3 \
  --output comparison.csv

This produces a combined CSV with all methods across all runs.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
TrajGRN-Bench's Python API is organized into several modules:

Module Description utils Utility functions and the methods registry API simulator Simulation drivers (Harissa, BoolODE, SERGIO) — see Development Guide post_analysis Metrics computation and visualization

docs.title: Methods Registry
docs.text:
The central registry API — the single source of truth for all method metadata.

from utils.methods_registry import get_registry, get_capabilities_table

# Load the full registry
registry = get_registry()

# Get capabilities as a DataFrame
caps = get_capabilities_table()
print(caps)

docs.title: Benchmark Runner
docs.text:
The config-driven benchmark orchestrator:

from benchmark_run_config import BenchmarkRunner

runner = BenchmarkRunner("configs/benchmark.example.yaml")
runner.run()

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Compute GRN and cell-level evaluation metrics:

from post_analysis.compute_metrics import compute_all_metrics

metrics = compute_all_metrics(
    methods_dir="benchmark/outputs_methods/my_run/",
    ground_truth_grn="benchmark/data/True/grn.csv",
    ground_truth_adata="benchmark/data/data_1.h5ad",
)

docs.title: Module Index
docs.text:
• utils — methods_registry, utils
  • simulator — common_config, Harissa, BoolODE, SERGIO (see Development Guide)
  • post_analysis — compute_metrics, metrics_grn, metrics_cells, visualizations

docs.title: post_analysis.compute_metrics
docs.text:
compute_metrics.py — Compute GRN and cell metrics for all outputs of a benchmark run.

For a given benchmark run (identified by global_run_name and run_type), this script: 1. Scans benchmark/outputs_methods/<global_run_name>_<run_type>/ for method folders and replicates. 2. Computes GRN metrics (precision, recall, F1, AUPRC, …) by comparing each method's data_<i>_GRN.npy against GRN_true/data_<i>_GRN.npy. 3. Computes cell metrics (Wasserstein, KL, …) by comparing each method's data_<i>_adata.h5ad against benchmark/data/data_<i>.h5ad. 4. Stores all results as CSV files under benchmark/outputs_metrics/<global_run_name>_<run_type>/, then generates visualizations.

Usage

python compute_metrics.py [options]

docs.title: compute_all_cell_metrics(run_dir, adata_dir, simulation, n_pca_components=50, ko_output_genes='none', resimulate_missing_ko=True)

docs.title: post_analysis.metrics_grn
docs.text:
metrics_grn.py — Gene Regulatory Network (GRN) evaluation metrics.

Provides functions to evaluate the similarity/distance between predicted and true GRNs: precision, recall, F1-score, AUPRC, Jaccard index, Hamming distance, Spearman correlation, and edge overlap.

Usage

from metrics_grn import compute_grn_metrics, load_grn

pred_grn = load_grn("path/to/predicted_grn.npy") true_grn = load_grn("path/to/true_grn.npy") metrics = compute_grn_metrics(pred_grn, true_grn)

docs.title: GRNMetricsError
docs.text:
Bases: Exception

Custom exception for GRN metrics specific errors.

docs.title: compute_precision_recall_curve(pred_grn, true_grn, threshold=0.0)
docs.text:
Compute precision-recall curve data for a predicted GRN against a ground-truth GRN.

The ground-truth GRN is binarized using threshold (edges with absolute weight ≥ threshold are considered present, excluding self-loops). The predicted GRN is used as a continuous score. Precision and recall are computed at all operating points via :func:sklearn.metrics.precision_recall_curve.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default pred_grn ndarray

Predicted GRN matrix (continuous scores).

required true_grn ndarray

Ground-truth GRN matrix (continuous or binary weights).

required threshold float

Binarization threshold for the true GRN.

0.0

Returns:

Type Description Dict[str, ndarray]

Dict with keys "precision", "recall", "thresholds" (arrays),

Dict[str, ndarray]

and "auprc" (float).

docs.title: post_analysis.metrics_cells
docs.text:
Metrics for evaluating cell population similarity.

Provides functions to compute Wasserstein distance, KL/Jensen-Shannon divergence, ARI, gene-gene correlation, and top-DE-gene overlap between predicted and true cell populations.

docs.title: plot_cell_umaps(run_dir, adata_dir, output_dir, n_pca_components=_DEFAULT_PCA_COMPONENTS, ko_output_genes='none', simulation='false', train_tps=None)
docs.text:
UMAP scatter plots of predicted vs true cell populations for every (method, replicate) pair.

The UMAP reducer is fitted once on the true adata per (replicate, perturbation) pair and reused across all methods via transform(). This guarantees that conserved training cells appear at the same UMAP coordinates in every panel — both within a (pred, true) pair and across different methods.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default run_dir Path

Path to benchmark/outputs_methods/<run_name>/.

required adata_dir Path

Directory containing true data_<i>.h5ad files.

required output_dir Path

Directory for saved PNG files.

required n_pca_components int

PCA components before UMAP reduction.

_DEFAULT_PCA_COMPONENTS ko_output_genes str

KO filter ("none", "all", or gene list).

'none' simulation str

Simulation mode identifier.

'false' train_tps Optional[List[float]]

Training-timepoint values. Cells whose timepoint falls in this list are considered conserved training cells and are drawn with hollow markers at reduced alpha so they can be distinguished from predicted cells.

None

Returns:

Type Description List[Path]

List of saved figure paths.

docs.text:
Scatter plots of gene-pair correlations: predicted vs true, for every (method, replicate) pair.

For each pair of expression matrices, computes the gene‑gene correlation matrix, extracts the upper triangle of unique gene pairs, and plots the predicted gene‑pair correlations against the true ones. The correlation‑of‑correlations :math:R is reported in the plot title — this is the same scalar returned by :func:metrics_cells.compute_gene_corr.

docs.title: plot_grn_pr_curves(run_dir, output_dir, threshold=0.0)
docs.text:
Precision-Recall curves for every (method, replicate) pair with a matching ground-truth GRN.

Each plot shows the PR curve and includes the AUPRC value in the legend. The diagonal dashed line represents the baseline (random classifier) which equals the fraction of positive edges.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default run_dir Path

Path to benchmark/outputs_methods/<run_name>/.

required output_dir Path

Directory for saved PNG files.

required threshold float

Binarization threshold for the true GRN.

0.0

Returns:

Type Description List[Path]

List of saved figure paths.

docs.title: utils.methods_registry
docs.text:
methods_registry.py — Read-only API for methods_registry.yaml.

Provides the canonical source of method metadata for all Python consumers (benchmark_run_config.py, ranking_table.py, compute_metrics.py, etc.).

Usage

from utils.methods_registry import ( load_registry, get_method, list_method_keys, get_entrypoint, get_execution, get_capabilities, get_capabilities_table, get_iteration_order, get_default_methods_json, export_execution_json, export_registry_json, )

registry = load_registry()

docs.title: Look up a single method
docs.text: method = get_method("FLeCS") print(method["entrypoint"]["script"]) # methods/flecs/flecs_train.py

docs.title: Get capabilities as a dict (for ranking_table.py)
docs.text: caps = get_capabilities_table() # {name: {grn_inference: True, ...}}

docs.title: Export execution config as JSON (for BENCHMARK_EXECUTION_JSON)
docs.text: exec_json = export_execution_json()

docs.title: get_method(key)
docs.text: Return the full metadata dict for a method, or raise KeyError.

docs.title: get_capabilities_table()
docs.text: Return the capabilities dict in the format expected by ranking_table.py: {method_key: {grn_inference: bool, trajectory_reconstruction: bool, perturbation_training: bool}}
